sources.outlet: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, 2025 National Veteran Suicide Prevention Annual Report, Part 2
sources.quote: Concurrently, rates rose for both male Recent Veteran VHA Users (+3.0%) and male Veterans who were not Recent Veteran VHA users (+2.7%).
sources.searcher_note: VA's own report, 2022-23 only. Table 6: male VHA users age-adjusted 51.5 (2022) to 53.0 (2023), 43.1 in 2001; male other veterans 38.4 to 39.4, 23.0 in 2001. Also: 2022-23 age-adjusted rate fell 2.3% for male non-veterans. No 2018 baseline by VHA use in the text. Date is approximate: news coverage says released Thursday before 2026-02-06.

sources.quote: From 2001 to 2023, the age-adjusted suicide rates for male veterans without recent VHA use rose by 71.1%, while it only rose 23% for those who had been recently seen by VA.
sources.searcher_note: Reports the VHA-use split for male veterans, but over 2001-2023, not 2018-2023; says both rose, non-users faster. Also gives 2023 age rates: 47.9 for 18-34, 37.3 for 35-54.

sources.quote: the rate among those enrolled in VA health care is less than half the rate of those who aren't in VA care.
sources.searcher_note: Possible disagreement: says VA-enrolled veterans have less than half the suicide rate of those outside VA care. VA's Table 6 shows the opposite for recent VHA users (male 53.0 vs 39.4, age-adjusted). 'Enrolled' vs 'recent user' definitions may differ. Not sex-specific.

sources.quote: It found that the suicide rate increased for both men and women, from 37.3 to to 37.8 for the former and from 13.7 to 13.9 for the latter.
sources.searcher_note: Male veteran crude rate 2022 to 2023 rose while total suicide count fell (6,442 to 6,398). No VHA-use split. The doubled 'to to' is on the page.

sources.quote: The suicide rate per 100,000 veterans was 35.2, marking the report's highest level dating back to 2018 (33).
sources.searcher_note: All-veteran rate 2018-2023 rise; says men rose 37.3 to 37.8; 61% of 2023 decedents not in VA care. No VHA-use rate split, no male 2018-23 comparison.

sources.quote: Veterans ages 18 to 34 die by suicide at a rate of 49.6 per 100,000, the highest of any age group.
sources.searcher_note: Only post-2026-06-30 item found; NGO blog restating VA report numbers. Does not report the male VHA-user vs non-user 2018-23 trend. Weak.

notes: The lead's own caveat says it is VA's published appendix; the VA report itself (and trade/news write-ups of it) reports male VHA-user and non-user age-adjusted rates both rising, but for 2001-23 (+23.0% vs +71.1%) and 2022-23 (+3.0% vs +2.7%), never 2018-23. VA's 2023 figures (53.0 VHA users, 39.4 others) differ slightly from the lead's 53.4 and 39.71 (lead likely uses the data appendix). No source found stating the ~10% 2018-23 rise for both groups, that non-veteran men were flat 2018-23, or that under-55s carry the rise. Military Times says VA-enrolled veterans' rate is less than half of non-enrolled, which runs opposite to VA's own recent-user table. Part 1 of the report (https://www.mentalhealth.va.gov/docs/data-sheets/2025/2025_National_Veteran_Suicide_Prevention_Annual_Report_PART_1_FINAL.pdf) has a 2018-2023 table: male veteran crude rate 35.0 to 37.8, no VHA split. RAND perspective 'The Rising Rate of Suicide Among Veterans' was 403 to fetch; not recorded. No new VA data (2024) found as of search.
